description: Reconstructed/iterated, NOT the pre-change experiment text; ungated — see split-a-strong-comm-poor-grammar. Split A: strong communication (developed, relevant, opinions with reasons) but frequent basic grammar errors — the QoL-under-penalisation defect case from the plan's own text. Embeds the plan's exact audible-error phrases verbatim ('moi je faire', 'on jouer', 'on regarder', 'je aime', 'préfère … que' ×2) plus the inaudible-as-ASR items the plan says are correctly NOT errors ('deux croissant', 'plein de chose', missing accents, 'meilleur amie'). Baseline QoL was 11/15 in 3/3 runs pre-change (single-call judge called these 'minor slips', a phrase absent from the QoL descriptors). The full pre-change Communication figure and the exact original transcript text were given in an earlier chat message, not logged in verification-log.md, and are unavailable in this session — this transcript is reconstructed from the plan's own quoted phrases, not copied from that message. Iterated once: the first reconstruction's ~6 audible errors landed post-change QoL in a 7-11 spread (borderline between 'frequent' and 'some'), so a few more instances of the same error types (still only the plan's named categories: infinitive-for-conjugated verb, 'préfère … que') were added to land more reliably in the frequent-errors band, not to change how the judge reads frequency. This iteration is exactly why this fixture was withdrawn as gate evidence this session.
